# dsh-context-usage-guard

Keeps the DeepSeek Harness composer's context-usage ring honest: an empty usage
sample during a retr

y no longer collapses it to `0%`, and its percentage is
typeset at the size of the figures beside it

.
**English** | 简体中文

A DeepSeek Harness (dsh)
plugin that repairs two defects in the composer's **context-usage ring** —

one in
the value it shows, one in how large that value is drawn:

1. the ring stops dropping to `0%` while a model request is being retried — the
host half; and
2. th

e ring's percentage renders at the size of every other figure on its own
line — the browser half, on

e renders at the size of every other figure on its own
line — the browser half, one stylesheet rule.
## The two bugs it repairs
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### The ring collapses to `0%` while a request is being retried

The ring renders the session projection `contextPressure`. That projection takes
the **newest usage
sample** as the current prompt size and publishes:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

A model call that fails before the provider reports anything — a `429`, a rate
limit, a timeout, a t

ransport error, or a user cancellation — still ends its
stream with a `usage` chunk:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The adapter's accumulator starts at zero and nothing ever overwrote it, so this
sample is *empty*, n

ot a measurement. But it is the newest sample, so
`pressureTokens` becomes `0`, and because the samp

le is stamped at the current
surface total the projection publishes `projectedTokens: 0`. `@deepseek

-ai/dsh-llm-retry`
then retries the same step — six times in the session this plugin was written
fro

m — and the ring reads `0%` for the whole storm, misreporting a context that
never changed.

Measured against the shipped `contextPressure` fold, replaying that session's
real events (`test/fol

inst the shipped `contextPressure` fold, replaying that session's
real events (`test/fold.spec.ts`):
| Replay | `pressureTokens` | `projectedTokens` | Ring |

| after the last successful call, before the retry | 64 389 | 64 389 | `6%` |
| the failed attempt,

**unguarded** | 0 | 0 | `0%` ← the symptom |
| the failed attempt, **guarded** | 64 389 | 64 389 | `

6%` |
| the retried step finally succeeds | 64 575 | 64 575 | `6%` |
### The percentage is one pixel larger than the figures beside it

The same footer band holds the session statistics and the ring, and the two
shipped stylesheets disa
gree by one pixel about how big a figure is:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Both prefixes are content-hashed per build — the pair above is what the
`0.2.2-rc.1` packages instal

led here carry; the *declarations* are what matters,
and `test/meter-typography.spec.ts` re-reads th

em from the installed packages
rather than trusting this block.

So `30%` renders about 8% larger than the `182 steps`, `238 tok/s`, `33.4M tok`
and `Cache hit 94%`

beside it, which reads as a different typeface. Measured on a
[该节后续省略]
## What the plugin does
| Half | Surface | What it does |
| Host | `llm/stream` waterfall | one listener that withholds an empty usage sample belonging to a f

ailed attempt, so the projection keeps its last real reading |
| Browser | the document `head` | one
self-tagged stylesheet rule that puts the meter's percentage at the statistics pills' figure size |

Neither half adds a page, a route, a settings section or a stored file. The host
half declares `inje

ct: ['llm']`, so the LLM service must exist first, and it
registers inside `ctx.effect`: cordis runs

the disposer on unload, when the
profile patch disables the row, or at shutdown — a bare `ctx.on` w

ould leak the
listener past unload.
One rule, applied to the chunk stream of every model call:

> A usage sample whose **every reported count is zero** measures nothing. When it
> belongs to an at

tempt that ended in `error` or `aborted`, it is dropped, so the
> previous real reading stands.
Everything else passes through untouched:

- **a successful completion**, whatever it reports — `stop`, `tool-calls` and
`max-tokens` are autho

hat did report something** — a partial call can carry real
input counts, so no billed counter is eve

; visible deltas keep their order and the terminal `finish` the retry
executor reads is preserved.
## Requirements
| Requirement | Version | Notes |
| DeepSeek Harness | `>=0.2.2-rc.1 <0.2.3-0` | the `dsh` range this build is pinned to (verified on
0.2.2-rc.1); peers are `@deepseek-ai/cordis` ~4.1.0, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm` 0.2.2-rc.1 and `@deepsee

k-ai/schemastery` ~3.19.0 |
| Node.js | `>=24.9.0` | `engines.node` in `package.json` |
| pnpm | `11

.20.0` | only for developing this repository: `pnpm check` and `pnpm build` |
| Google Chrome, Chrom
ium or Edge | any recent | only for `tools/preview.mjs`, the screenshot harness |

The built halves are committed in `lib/`, so installing the plugin needs no build
step and no toolch
ain beyond the harness you install it into.
## What this plugin deliberately does not do

- **It does not touch the projection registry.** `dsh-token-meter` registers
`contextPressure` inter

nally and the registry *shares* a key rather than
replacing it, so a second registration cannot over

ride the fold, and
re-registering the same key first would hijack a package this plugin does not
own

. Repairing the fold's input is the narrow fix; the fold itself is left to
its owners.
- **It does n

ot replace or restyle the ring's component.** The meter is rendered
inside `dsh-client-ui-conversati

on`'s input bar with no extension seat. The one
thing the browser half does is add a `font-size` dec

laration to the trigger the
statistics already prove is wrong; the ring, its icon, its colors, its h

over
state and its dialog are the shipped ones.
- **It does not invent a number.** When nothing meas

urable has ever been
reported, the projection stays absent and the ring stays hidden — the shipped
b

ehavior — rather than showing a value nobody measured.
- **It does not freeze the reading.** The nex

t successful attempt reports real
usage and the ring advances, which the suite asserts.
